jsonld.name: Mortgage Calculator
jsonld.description: Estimate a monthly mortgage payment including principal, interest, property tax, homeowners insurance, HOA and PMI, with fixed and 5/1 ARM options and a full amortization schedule.

mainEntity.name: How is a monthly mortgage payment calculated?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fixed-rate amortization for principal and interest, then monthly tax and insurance. Estimate only — not a lender quote.

mainEntity.name: Does this include PMI, HOA fees, or closing costs?

acceptedAnswer.text: HOA is optional. Estimated PMI appears below 20% down. Closing costs are not included.

mainEntity.name: How much house can I afford?

acceptedAnswer.text: A common starting point is 28–36% of gross income. Use the House Affordability Calculator.

mainEntity.name: Should I choose a 15-year or 30-year mortgage?

acceptedAnswer.text: 15-year usually costs less interest and more per month. 30-year keeps the payment lower. The 15-Year Fixed card above shows how much interest you'd save at your inputs.

mainEntity.name: Does a larger down payment lower my monthly payment?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. It reduces the loan amount and often removes PMI at 20% down.

mainEntity.name: Are these figures a formal loan offer?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Confirm rates and fees with a lender quote.

mainEntity.name: Should I pay extra on my mortgage or invest that money instead?

acceptedAnswer.text: On a $400,000 loan at 7%, $300/month extra saves $168,391 in interest and pays off 7.8 years early — a guaranteed 7% return. Investing the same $300/month at 8% would grow to ~$450,389 over the same period. See the full extra-payments-vs-investing breakdown for the math.

mainEntity.name: When exactly does PMI come off my loan?

acceptedAnswer.text: By federal law, PMI automatically ends at 78% of your home's original value; you can request removal yourself at 80%. This calculator drops PMI at the 78% point, and extra payments bring that date forward.
